content: The wish: from Claude Code, Codex, or any harness with bp configured, carry the current conversation into Barkpark and continue it on another machine with the same context. The design: a first-class session document opened at session start and kept alive as the work happens — one appended event per paper published, task closed, epic wave sealed, and git push — with a distilled synthesis refreshed at checkpoints, the scrubbed raw transcript attached as a media asset, and every touched task stamped with a reference back to its sessions. Crash safety is the point: a session that dies mid-flight never runs its close, but its event trail is already on the server.

SESSION LIFECYCLE (living document on the server)          RESUME (machine B)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────          ──────────────────
bp session open  ──► log ── log ── log ── … ──► checkpoint ──► close
   (at start,         │      │      │              │             │
    status:open,   paper    task   git push    synthesis     final synthesis
    metadata       published closed            refresh +     + final scrubbed
    seeded)                                    transcript    transcript,
                                               snapshot      status: closed
                                                                  │
/session-resume <slug> ◄──────────────────────────────────────────┘

content: The synthesis is the readable summary; the events are the ground truth between checkpoints. A resume of a crashed session — status still open, no final synthesis — stands on the trail: every paper, task, and push, each with a ref and a server timestamp.

A new content type with a portable-doc blocks body plus structured fields. Schema defined in code following the tasks/schema.ex pattern and registered by the Bulldocs plugin — sessions depend on paper machinery, which IS Bulldocs, so no new plugin. head: Field
Type
Notes
rows: working directory on the origin machine
commit SHA and branch at upload time
scrubbed JSONL; optional — synthesis-only sessions allowed
append-only trail {ts, kind, ref?, note?}; kinds: paper-published | task-closed | epic-wave-complete | push | note

content: The paper editor and ingest path are hard-gated to type == "paper" today. The gate widens to a blocks-type whitelist {paper, session} — never an open door. head: File
Change
rows: upsert_paper / apply_paper_block_op take a type param, default "paper" — existing callers unmoved
ingest + ops routes accept a whitelisted type; manifest gains the bp session verb group
accept + validate the type param; non-whitelist type → 422
editor dispatch (:415) and backlinks-open (:202) key on the whitelist — sessions open in the real paper pane
already generalized — wire the HTTP ops path through apply_document_block_op/4

content: One additive field on type:task — sessions, an array of references with refType session — plus POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions mirroring the existing /papers endpoint. Close stamps every task claimed, stamped, or closed during the conversation (belt-and-braces over the per-event task-closed logs). A task worked across three sessions references all three: full provenance of what conversation produced what work, and the session's event trail shows when in the session each task landed.

blocks.code:
bp session open <slug> --file meta.json         # create at session start: metadata, status: open
bp session log <slug> --kind <kind> [--ref <id>] [--note "…"]   # append one event (server stamps ts)
bp session publish <slug> --file session.json   # upsert synthesis blocks + metadata (checkpoint/close)
bp session view <slug>                          # read-back: metadata + events + synthesis blocks
bp session link-task <task-id> <slug>           # POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions

content: log is deliberately one cheap call — it must be frictionless enough to run after every milestone. Log failures are non-blocking: never fail a task close or a push because the session log call failed; warn loudly and continue.

.claude/skills/session/ — SKILL.md plus helpers/scrub.sh. The procedure is pure prose and bp CLI, so Codex can execute it from AGENTS.md. Open at session start seeds metadata and tags; the slug stays in conversation context. Per-milestone logging is agent-driven in v1, wired into the places milestones already happen:

head: Milestone
Where the log call is written in
rows: fleet-listener close step; session-completion checklist step 3
session-completion checklist step 4, after git push succeeds

items.value: Checkpoint, on demand and after big milestones — distill: the in-session model rewrites the synthesis blocks from the fixed template (current task · progress · key files · decisions · next steps · learnings) → bp session publish.
Locate the transcript, harness-aware: Claude Code at ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<uuid>.jsonl (connectors charter D135); Codex in its sessions dir. Not found → synthesis-only, said loudly.
Scrub via helpers/scrub.sh: bp_admin_*, Bearer tokens, BARKPARK_*_TOKEN values, GitHub ghp_*/github_pat_*, AWS AKIA* pairs, private-key blocks → [REDACTED]. Output to scratchpad, never in-repo.
Upload the scrubbed snapshot with bp media upload (100 MB cap — over-cap fails loud with split instructions, never truncates silently); update the transcript ref.
Close, at session end: final checkpoint + status: closed + stamp every touched task with bp session link-task, then print the resume one-liner for the other machine.

content: Remove reliance on agent discipline for the events Barkpark itself witnesses: bp sends an X-Barkpark-Session header whenever a session is open (--session flag / BARKPARK_SESSION env / config binding), and the task-close and bulldocs-publish endpoints append the event server-side when the header is present. Git pushes stay agent-logged — Barkpark never sees them. Harness hooks remain out of scope: harness-specific plumbing for the least portability.

.claude/skills/session-resume/ — takes a slug. bp session view loads the synthesis, metadata, and event trail into context — the trail is ground truth for anything after the last checkpoint, so an open session with no synthesis still resumes from its events. Warns if cwd, repo, or branch mismatch the metadata, then marks the session status: resumed. The transcript is offered as a /files/… URL for drill-down, never auto-downloaded. No-arg does nothing clever; the SKILL.md documents the one-liner query for listing recent sessions.

items.text: Session-first ordering: publish the session doc, then stamp tasks. A failed stamp enumerates the unlinked tasks instead of leaving silent gaps.
items.title: Nothing half-linked

items.text: A failed bp session log never aborts the milestone that triggered it — warn loudly, continue. The close-time task stamping backfills anything the per-event logs missed.
items.title: Non-blocking logs

items.text: Transcript missing or over the 100 MB cap → synthesis-only, recorded in the doc and shouted in the output. Resume of a nonexistent slug → fail loud + print the listing query. Wrong repo/branch on resume → warning, not a block. Crashed session (open, stale) → resume allowed; the event trail is the context.
items.title: Loud fallbacks

items.text: Ingest with type: session round-trips; non-whitelist type → 422; session log appends with server timestamp, rejects unknown kinds, events append-only; pane_builder dispatches session → paper pane; POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions appends and dedupes; existing paper paths regression-covered via the default param.
items.title: Elixir tests

items.text: Open at session start → log a paper-publish, a task-close, a push → checkpoint → close → resume in a fresh session against a local server; verify event trail, synthesis fidelity, transcript link, task backlinks. Crash case: open + logs, no close → resume works from the trail.
items.title: Skill smoke

items.value: Harness hooks for auto-logging (PostToolUse on git push etc.) — harness-specific, least portable.
Cross-server session sync or mirroring.
A custom Studio session pane — the paper pane IS the UI.
Auto-list in the resume skill — a documented query instead.
Diff/merge of concurrent sessions.
Server-side auto-log is NOT out of scope — it is v1.5, filed as a bp task and built next.

Design spec · approved 2026-07-25 · repo mirror: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-session-handoff-design.md

Session handoff: a living session document, resumable anywhere

The wish: from Claude Code, Codex, or any harness with bp configured, carry the current conversation into Barkpark and continue it on another machine with the same context. The design: a first-class session document opened at session start and kept alive as the work happens — one appended event per paper published, task closed, epic wave sealed, and git push — with a distilled synthesis refreshed at checkpoints, the scrubbed raw transcript attached as a media asset, and every touched task stamped with a reference back to its sessions. Crash safety is the point: a session that dies mid-flight never runs its close, but its event trail is already on the server.

Decisions

QuestionDecision
PayloadBoth, linked — distilled synthesis is the primary document; scrubbed raw transcript attached
Content modelFirst-class session type — blocks body, opens in the paper editor; server-side generalization included
Capture cadenceEvent-driven living document — opened at start, one logged event per milestone, checkpointed synthesis, explicit close. Not command-only.
Logging mechanismAgent discipline in v1 (skills, workflows, and checklists instruct the log calls); server-side auto-log is the filed next step
Task linkageTasks reference the sessions they were worked in (sessions[] on type:task)
ResumeFull skill pair: session lifecycle skill + session-resume
Target serverWhatever the project's active bp context points at — no pinning
SecretsPattern-scrub the transcript before upload, no confirm step
CLI surfaceDedicated bp session verb group

The lifecycle

The synthesis is the readable summary; the events are the ground truth between checkpoints. A resume of a crashed session — status still open, no final synthesis — stands on the trail: every paper, task, and push, each with a ref and a server timestamp.

The session type

A new content type with a portable-doc blocks body plus structured fields. Schema defined in code following the tasks/schema.ex pattern and registered by the Bulldocs plugin — sessions depend on paper machinery, which IS Bulldocs, so no new plugin. Slug convention: session-YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>. Session docs do not list their tasks; backlinks give the reverse view from the task-side references.

FieldTypeNotes
titlestringrequired
harnessstring enumclaude-code | codex | other
session_uuidstringharness-native session id
cwdstringworking directory on the origin machine
machinestringhostname of the origin machine
git_head / git_branchstringcommit SHA and branch at upload time
started_at / ended_atdatetimesession bounds
transcriptreference → mediaAssetscrubbed JSONL; optional — synthesis-only sessions allowed
statusstring enumopen | closed | resumed | superseded
eventsarrayOf objectappend-only trail {ts, kind, ref?, note?}; kinds: paper-published | task-closed | epic-wave-complete | push | note

Generalizing the paper machinery

The paper editor and ingest path are hard-gated to type == "paper" today. The gate widens to a blocks-type whitelist {paper, session} — never an open door. Content.apply_document_block_op/4 is already the generalization; the HTTP ops path gets wired through it for non-paper types. The publish wall (non-trivial description + published tags) applies to sessions exactly as to papers; the lifecycle skill supplies both at open.

FileChange
api/lib/barkpark/content/papers.exupsert_paper / apply_paper_block_op take a type param, default "paper" — existing callers unmoved
api/lib/barkpark/plugins/bulldocs.exingest + ops routes accept a whitelisted type; manifest gains the bp session verb group
api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_ingest_controller.exaccept + validate the type param; non-whitelist type → 422
api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/pane_builder.exeditor dispatch (:415) and backlinks-open (:202) key on the whitelist — sessions open in the real paper pane
api/lib/barkpark/content/papers/block_ops.exalready generalized — wire the HTTP ops path through apply_document_block_op/4

Tasks remember their sessions

One additive field on type:task — sessions, an array of references with refType session — plus POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions mirroring the existing /papers endpoint. Close stamps every task claimed, stamped, or closed during the conversation (belt-and-braces over the per-event task-closed logs). A task worked across three sessions references all three: full provenance of what conversation produced what work, and the session's event trail shows when in the session each task landed.

The bp session verbs

log is deliberately one cheap call — it must be frictionless enough to run after every milestone. Log failures are non-blocking: never fail a task close or a push because the session log call failed; warn loudly and continue.

The lifecycle skill

.claude/skills/session/ — SKILL.md plus helpers/scrub.sh. The procedure is pure prose and bp CLI, so Codex can execute it from AGENTS.md. Open at session start seeds metadata and tags; the slug stays in conversation context. Per-milestone logging is agent-driven in v1, wired into the places milestones already happen:

MilestoneWhere the log call is written in
Paper publishedpaper-publish procedure (papers cheatsheet note)
Task closedfleet-listener close step; session-completion checklist step 3
Epic wave completebp-epic-cycle workflow, wave seal step
Git pushsession-completion checklist step 4, after git push succeeds
1. Checkpoint, on demand and after big milestones — distill: the in-session model rewrites the synthesis blocks from the fixed template (current task · progress · key files · decisions · next steps · learnings) → bp session publish.
2. Locate the transcript, harness-aware: Claude Code at ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<uuid>.jsonl (connectors charter D135); Codex in its sessions dir. Not found → synthesis-only, said loudly.
3. Scrub via helpers/scrub.sh: bp_admin_*, Bearer tokens, BARKPARK_*_TOKEN values, GitHub ghp_*/github_pat_*, AWS AKIA* pairs, private-key blocks → [REDACTED]. Output to scratchpad, never in-repo.
4. Upload the scrubbed snapshot with bp media upload (100 MB cap — over-cap fails loud with split instructions, never truncates silently); update the transcript ref.
5. Close, at session end: final checkpoint + status: closed + stamp every touched task with bp session link-task, then print the resume one-liner for the other machine.

Remove reliance on agent discipline for the events Barkpark itself witnesses: bp sends an X-Barkpark-Session header whenever a session is open (--session flag / BARKPARK_SESSION env / config binding), and the task-close and bulldocs-publish endpoints append the event server-side when the header is present. The resume skill

.claude/skills/session-resume/ — takes a slug. bp session view loads the synthesis, metadata, and event trail into context — the trail is ground truth for anything after the last checkpoint, so an open session with no synthesis still resumes from its events. Warns if cwd, repo, or branch mismatch the metadata, then marks the session status: resumed. The transcript is offered as a /files/… URL for drill-down, never auto-downloaded. Error handling and testing

Nothing half-linked
Session-first ordering: publish the session doc, then stamp tasks. A failed stamp enumerates the unlinked tasks instead of leaving silent gaps.
Non-blocking logs
A failed bp session log never aborts the milestone that triggered it — warn loudly, continue. The close-time task stamping backfills anything the per-event logs missed.
Loud fallbacks
Transcript missing or over the 100 MB cap → synthesis-only, recorded in the doc and shouted in the output. Resume of a nonexistent slug → fail loud + print the listing query. Wrong repo/branch on resume → warning, not a block. Crashed session (open, stale) → resume allowed; the event trail is the context.
Elixir tests
Ingest with type: session round-trips; non-whitelist type → 422; session log appends with server timestamp, rejects unknown kinds, events append-only; pane_builder dispatches session → paper pane; POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions appends and dedupes; existing paper paths regression-covered via the default param.
Skill smoke
Open at session start → log a paper-publish, a task-close, a push → checkpoint → close → resume in a fresh session against a local server; verify event trail, synthesis fidelity, transcript link, task backlinks. Crash case: open + logs, no close → resume works from the trail.

Out of scope (YAGNI)

• Harness hooks for auto-logging (PostToolUse on git push etc.) — harness-specific, least portable.
• Cross-server session sync or mirroring.
• A custom Studio session pane — the paper pane IS the UI.
• Auto-list in the resume skill — a documented query instead.
• Diff/merge of concurrent sessions.
• Server-side auto-log is NOT out of scope — it is v1.5, filed as a bp task and built next.

api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_ingest_controller.exaccept + validate the type param; non-whitelist type → 422
api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/pane_builder.exeditor dispatch (:415) and backlinks-open (:202) key on the whitelist — sessions open in the real paper pane
api/lib/barkpark/content/papers/block_ops.exalready generalized — wire the HTTP ops path through apply_document_block_op/4
Tasks remember their sessions
One additive field on type:task — sessions, an array of references with refType session — plus POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions mirroring the existing /papers endpoint. Close stamps every task claimed, stamped, or closed during the conversation (belt-and-braces over the per-event task-closed logs). A task worked across three sessions references all three: full provenance of what conversation produced what work, and the session's event trail shows when in the session each task landed.
The bp session verbs
log is deliberately one cheap call — it must be frictionless enough to run after every milestone. Log failures are non-blocking: never fail a task close or a push because the session log call failed; warn loudly and continue.
The lifecycle skill
.claude/skills/session/ — SKILL.md plus helpers/scrub.sh. The procedure is pure prose and bp CLI, so Codex can execute it from AGENTS.md. Open at session start seeds metadata and tags; the slug stays in conversation context. Per-milestone logging is agent-driven in v1, wired into the places milestones already happen:
MilestoneWhere the log call is written in
Paper publishedpaper-publish procedure (papers cheatsheet note)
Task closedfleet-listener close step; session-completion checklist step 3
Epic wave completebp-epic-cycle workflow, wave seal step
Git pushsession-completion checklist step 4, after git push succeeds
  1. Checkpoint, on demand and after big milestones — distill: the in-session model rewrites the synthesis blocks from the fixed template (current task · progress · key files · decisions · next steps · learnings) → bp session publish.
  2. Locate the transcript, harness-aware: Claude Code at ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<uuid>.jsonl (connectors charter D135); Codex in its sessions dir. Not found → synthesis-only, said loudly.
  3. Scrub via helpers/scrub.sh: bp_admin_*, Bearer tokens, BARKPARK_*_TOKEN values, GitHub ghp_*/github_pat_*, AWS AKIA* pairs, private-key blocks → [REDACTED]. Output to scratchpad, never in-repo.
  4. Upload the scrubbed snapshot with bp media upload (100 MB cap — over-cap fails loud with split instructions, never truncates silently); update the transcript ref.
  5. Close, at session end: final checkpoint + status: closed + stamp every touched task with bp session link-task, then print the resume one-liner for the other machine.
Toward auto-log (v1.5 — filed, built next)
Remove reliance on agent discipline for the events Barkpark itself witnesses: bp sends an X-Barkpark-Session header whenever a session is open (--session flag / BARKPARK_SESSION env / config binding), and the task-close and bulldocs-publish endpoints append the event server-side when the header is present. Git pushes stay agent-logged — Barkpark never sees them. Harness hooks remain out of scope: harness-specific plumbing for the least portability.
The resume skill
.claude/skills/session-resume/ — takes a slug. bp session view loads the synthesis, metadata, and event trail into context — the trail is ground truth for anything after the last checkpoint, so an open session with no synthesis still resumes from its events. Warns if cwd, repo, or branch mismatch the metadata, then marks the session status: resumed. The transcript is offered as a /files/… URL for drill-down, never auto-downloaded. No-arg does nothing clever; the SKILL.md documents the one-liner query for listing recent sessions.
Error handling and testing
Nothing half-linked
Session-first ordering: publish the session doc, then stamp tasks. A failed stamp enumerates the unlinked tasks instead of leaving silent gaps.
Non-blocking logs
A failed bp session log never aborts the milestone that triggered it — warn loudly, continue. The close-time task stamping backfills anything the per-event logs missed.
Loud fallbacks
Transcript missing or over the 100 MB cap → synthesis-only, recorded in the doc and shouted in the output. Resume of a nonexistent slug → fail loud + print the listing query. Wrong repo/branch on resume → warning, not a block. Crashed session (open, stale) → resume allowed; the event trail is the context.
Elixir tests
Ingest with type: session round-trips; non-whitelist type → 422; session log appends with server timestamp, rejects unknown kinds, events append-only; pane_builder dispatches session → paper pane; POST /v1/tasks/:id/sessions appends and dedupes; existing paper paths regression-covered via the default param.
Skill smoke
Open at session start → log a paper-publish, a task-close, a push → checkpoint → close → resume in a fresh session against a local server; verify event trail, synthesis fidelity, transcript link, task backlinks. Crash case: open + logs, no close → resume works from the trail.
Out of scope (YAGNI)
  • Harness hooks for auto-logging (PostToolUse on git push etc.) — harness-specific, least portable.
  • Cross-server session sync or mirroring.
  • A custom Studio session pane — the paper pane IS the UI.
  • Auto-list in the resume skill — a documented query instead.
  • Diff/merge of concurrent sessions.
  • Server-side auto-log is NOT out of scope — it is v1.5, filed as a bp task and built next.
description: Approved design for carrying an agent conversation across machines: a first-class session content type kept alive as the work happens — opened at session start, appending an event per paper published, task closed, epic wave sealed, and git push — with checkpointed synthesis, a scrubbed-transcript attachment, task-side session references, a bp session verb group, and a resume skill. Agent-discipline logging in v1; server-side auto-log filed as the next step.
